decision.title: XSLT backwards compatible behaviour and XPath 1.0 compatibility mode (packet )
decision.summary: is one static context flag that makes the lowering insert XPath 1.0 conversions, set for XSLT elements whose effective version is below 2.0, with no second evaluator.

body.p: , after , , , . Replaces 's place for XSLT 1.0 behaviour (asks_xslt_1_behaviour and its XTDE0160 in src/xslt_lower.c).

item.p: One flag, no second evaluator: XPath 1.0 compatibility mode is has_xpath_1_compatibility_mode of the XPath static context (src/xpath_static_internal.h) and, additively, the last field of sxml_static_context_configuration (xpath.h; XPath hosts only, XQuery has no such mode and ignores it). The lowering reads it and inserts the 1.0 conversions as STATIC_CALLs of internal native rows in no function table (src/xpath_compatibility.c, golden file src/xslt_simple_content.c); the evaluator does not know the mode.

Arguments of static calls to built-in functions (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1): the first item; then fn:string for xs:string and xs:string?, fn:number for xs:double and xs:double? (the optional forms keep ()); fn:concat takes xs:string($v[1]) per argument (F&O 4.0). Not for partial applications, dynamic calls, stylesheet functions (XSLT 4.0, 10.3.2) or the lowering's own calls.

Arithmetic and unary operands (4.9): atomized, the first item, () as NaN, xs:boolean, xs:string, xs:decimal, xs:float and xs:untypedAtomic by fn:number. The operands of "to" keep their first items (4.8.2 coerces them).

General comparisons (4.11.2): one row does the mode's rules: the xs:boolean rule (EBV of the other operand), fn:number of every item for <, <=, >, >=; for = and != a pair with a numeric item compares as doubles, other pairs by the mode-false rules. It calls the existing sxml_operator_make_general_comparison on the converted parts.

XSLT: the static context of every element whose effective version is below 2.0 has the mode (5.3.1, 3.8.1; 2.0 and 3.0 behaviour is 4.0's). The 1.0 rules of the instructions, each where the instruction is lowered, through sxml_xslt_lowering_has_xslt_1_behaviour and sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_first_atom (fn:head(fn:data(.))): xsl:value-of with select and no separator (11.4.2), attribute value templates (5.6.1; not text value templates), xsl:number value (12.2: first item, () as NaN, an unconvertible value formatted as "NaN" between the format's prefix and suffix), xsl:sort keys (13.1.2, first item after data-type), keys in backwards compatible mode (20.2.2: use values and fn:key's argument cast to xs:string), and an unknown extension function bound to a fallback error function, XTDE1425 when called (3.8.1, 24.1.2; function-available stays false). supports-backwards-compatibility is yes.

xs:numeric is not xs:double (XPath 4.0, 3.4.1 names xs:double only; F&O 4.0's changes list says strings are no longer accepted where the type became xs:numeric): fn:format-number, fn:round, fn:floor and fn:abs do not convert strings or () by fn:number in the mode. The suites expect the older conversion: XT40 format-number 014, 035, 038-041, backwards-022, version-021, xpath-compat-0302 and 0401, and QT4 numberformat15, 38, 41, 42 fail. Not reclassified ().

Not done: the expressions of a text value template in a 1.0 element are still lowered with the mode (3.8.1 asks for it off; only expand-text="yes" on a 1.0 element meets it); the default output method xml for a 1.0 stylesheet is also used for an explicit xsl:result-document (backwards-019b); exsl:node-set, which DocBook's 1.0 stylesheets call (docbook-001 raises XTDE1425; it needs a function namespace sxml_well_known_namespace lacks); docbook-002 meets an XPST0003 in an included module.

Drivers: XT40 supports backwards_compatibility and keeps it among 's non-goals, as XML_1.1 (); QT4 supports xpath-1.0-compatibility for XPath only and sets the mode for the test cases that ask for it (assertions stay mode false), also kept out of the denominator. The three XT40 cases that expect XTDE0160 (and three more asking for the feature unsatisfied) are not run now.

Numbers (release, XT40 whole, case by case): 8,687 to 8,787 passed at 3dc364a; 111 of the 124 cases (89.5 %, gate 80 %); QT4 xpath-1.0-compatibility 1 of 5 (generate-id-018; the other four are the xs:numeric cases above). Unit test tests/xslt_compatibility_test.c.

sources.source: XT40 passes, whole suite, case by case, and the backwards-compatibility cases
